body:
### Describe the bug

1. If a user installs a profiling function with `sys.setprofile` and Cython isn't configured to use `sys.monitoring`, Cython directly calls the installed profiling function with a `PyFrameObject` that's not on the actual Python stack, but which references a code object containing the function name / file name / line number of the Cython function. A profiler can look at the passed frame's code and figure out what Cython function was called. This case works fine.

2. If a user installs a profiling function with `sys.monitoring.register_callback` and Cython is configured to use `sys.monitoring`, Cython calls `PyMonitoring_FirePyStartEvent` with a code object containing the function name / file name / line number of the Cython function. A profiler can look at the code object it receives and figure out what Cython function was called. This case works fine.

3. If a user installs a profiling function with `sys.setprofile` and Cython is configured to use `sys.monitoring`, Cython calls `PyMonitoring_FirePyStartEvent` with a code object containing the function name / file name / line number of the Cython function. CPython has a compatibility hook for legacy tracers that _completely ignores_ the received code object and instead passes the top frame of the Python stack to the function installed by `sys.setprofile`. The profiling function has no way of figuring out what Cython function was called. This case is completely broken.

I'm not sure whether this should be considered a CPython bug or a Cython bug, but either way it's something that certainly isn't working as intended...

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

Write a Cython function that has profiler integration enabled:

```cython
cimport cython

@cython.profile(True)
def cython_func():
    func()
```

And note that on modern Cython versions on Python 3.13 and higher, no frame referencing this function ever gets passed to a profile function installed by `sys.setprofile`. Instead, the frame calling the Cython function is passed twice.

### Expected behaviour

Either the profiling function installed by `sys.setprofile` shouldn't be called when Cython is using `sys.monitoring`, or it should be called with a frame object that holds a code object referring to the Cython file name / function name / line number.

### OS

Linux

### Python version

3.14.3

### Cython version

3.3.0

### Additional context

See https://github.com/bloomberg/memray/issues/1037

comment_data.body:
This could be fixed by CPython checking whether the code object that the monitoring callback receives is the code object held by the top frame of the Python stack, and refusing to call the `tstate->c_profilefunc` if not.

Or it could be fixed by CPython detecting that condition and creating a fake frame to pass to the `c_profilefunc`.

Or it could be fixed by Cython falling back to _not_ using `sys.monitoring` whenever `tstate->c_profilefunc` is set.

Of those 3 fixes, I think the last one is probably best - not least because Cython uses `sys.monitoring` for Python 3.13, which will _very soon_ be out of bugfix support.

Perhaps I should report this to CPython as well, in the hopes that, if the CPython core devs agree this is a CPython bug, the fix might wind up backported into the final 3.13 bugfix release...

> Or it could be fixed by Cython falling back to not using `sys.monitoring` whenever `tstate->c_profilefunc` is set.

The choice of monitoring vs/legacy profiling is a compile-time option for us so I don't think there's any chance of detecting at runtime and falling back to the legacy profiling. Turning it off completely might be an option though.

> not least because Cython uses sys.monitoring for Python 3.13, which will very soon be out of bugfix support.

Think you might be slightly late on that one... https://discuss.python.org/t/python-3-10-22-3-11-17-3-12-15-3-13-16-and-3-14-8-are-now-available/109296/5

------------------------------------

From reading the issue memray issue. Is it:
* you still use the legacy profiling mode to implement memray
* you have existing code designed to ignore Cython frames (because it isn't the aim of your tool)
* but Cython with `sys.monitoring` is "causing" spurious events that look like Python calls to fire

?

I'm just trying to make sure I understand the desired outcome correctly.

> Think you might be slightly late on that one...

☹️ Oh well.

> * you still use the legacy profiling mode to implement memray

Yes, for now.

> * you have existing code designed to ignore Cython frames (because it isn't the aim of your tool)

Yes, we ignore Cython frames, but not because it isn't the aim of the tool, but because it was difficult to support them, for at least two different reasons.

1. We support installing the Memray tracker programmatically, possibly after the application being profiled has spawned some threads already. To report accurate stacks for allocations performed by threads that existed before we installed our profile function, we grab the stack for every existing thread when tracking starts, by looking at the each threadstate's current frame and then walking the frame linked list back. That won't find the Cython frames, so if a thread was in the middle of a call to a Cython function when tracking started, we'd see a profiling event saying control has returned from a function that was never on our stack. Handling that proved to be tricky.

2. We support reporting hybrid stacks that include both the Python frames and the native C/C++/Rust/etc frames, and that requires us to be able to pair up the native stack with the Python stack. The extra frames that Cython reports to the profiling / monitoring function make it harder for us to pair up those stacks. We have to be able to recognize that they're not normal Python frames and so they don't replace a call to `_PyEval_EvalFrameDefault` but some other function, and then we need to know which native frames represent the evaluation of that Cython function so we can replace the right thing.

We originally supported it, in a way that was sort of hacky (looking for filenames ending in `.pyx`, which didn't work well when Cython added its pure-Python mode) but dropped our support in https://github.com/bloomberg/memray/pull/206 after realizing it was costing us lots of maintenance effort for minimal benefit, because most Cython wheels aren't built with profiling support enabled anyway, and because if people want to know what's happening inside extension modules they can run Memray in `--native` mode and find not just what Cython functions were called but also what C functions were called by those Cython functions.

> * but Cython with `sys.monitoring` is "causing" spurious events that look like Python calls to fire

But that's right. I think this is really a CPython bug, tbh - `PyMonitoring_FirePyStartEvent` just doesn't work correctly with a `sys.setprofile` profile function, it's entirely broken by design and no one noticed until now. It works fine with `sys.monitoring` tools, which is what it was tested with, but doesn't work at all with the legacy `sys.monitoring` tools that CPython uses to implement `sys.setprofile` and `set.settrace` these days.

For our desired outcome, anything that stops our profile function from getting incorrect calls would be great. If that's recognizing that a `sys.setprofile` function is installed and disabling profiling support instead of calling `PyMonitoring_FirePyStartEvent`, I think that would be great - it is completely broken, so I don't think anything meaningful is lost by doing that. I could also live with us having some way to set a flag somewhere that asks Cython to stop emitting profiling events because our profiler doesn't want them, though I can't see a nice way to do that. The problem might just go away if we switch to use `sys.monitoring` instead of `sys.setprofile`, too, so if you're unwilling to work around the CPython bug and the CPython core devs aren't willing to fix it, then that might be the only option Memray is left with...

> I think this is really a CPython bug, tbh - `PyMonitoring_FirePyStartEvent` just doesn't work correctly with a `sys.setprofile` profile function

Yeah I agree with this.

I think I'd like to wait a little bit just to see if there's any conclusion reached on the CPython side. But I suspect the likely outcome is that we should do what you suggest and avoid calling the legacy profiling function. We might have to check if both the legacy function and `sys.monitoring` callbacks can be enabled at the same time though...

> We might have to check if both the legacy function and `sys.monitoring` callbacks can be enabled at the same time though...

Unfortunately, they can be. But I think losing profiling of Cython functions entirely, as though the extension module wasn't compiled with `profile=True`, is less bad than sending completely incorrect stuff to the `sys.setprofile` profile function, so I think that Cython's profiling support should probably be disabled whenever there's a `sys.setprofile` function, even if `sys.monitoring` callbacks exist.

That said, hopefully the CPython folks agree that this is a bug - it seems obvious to me that it is - and if so, maybe it'll get fixed for 3.14 and 3.15, and Cython will only need to check for a `sys.setprofile` function and disable the calls to `PyMonitoring_FirePyStartEvent` for 3.13 - that wouldn't be so bad...
